title: ‘चिताको ज्वाला’ कथामा समाख्यानशास्त्र
nepali: प्रस्तुत आलेख गुरुप्रसाद मैनालीद्वारा लिखित ‘चिताको ज्वाला’ कथामा समाख्यानशास्त्रीय सैद्धान्तिक अवधारणाको विश्लेषणसँग सम्बद्ध छ । यसमा समाख्याताको पहिचान कसरी गरिएको छ, समाख्यानात्मक वाच्यत्व कुन रुपमा प्रकट भएको छ । समाख्यानात्मक केन्द्रणलाई कस्तो रुपमा प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ भन्ने जिज्ञासाको समाधान खोज्न प्रयत्न गरिएको छ । यसमा समाख्यानशास्त्रसम्बन्धी सैद्धान्तिक मान्यताका आधारमा कथाको विश्लेषण गरिएको हुँदा निगमनात्मक विधिको उपयोग गरिएको छ । यसमा के भनिएको छ र कसले भनेको हो भन्ने विषयको पहिचान गरिएको छ । समाख्याता पाठभित्र छ कि बाहिर छ वा आफै पात्रको रूपमा उपस्थित छ वा अरुलाई उपस्थित गराएको छ भन्ने कुराको खोजी गरिएको छ । पाठमा समाख्याता द्रष्टा वा भोक्ता कुन रूपमा वा दुवै रूपमा रहेको छ भन्ने कुराको निक्र्योल गरिएको छ । यसरी प्रस्तुत अध्ययनमा मैनालीको ‘चिताको ज्वाला’ कथामा समाख्याता प्रथम पुरुष, प्रथाम पुरुषमा पनि परकथानात्मक, खुल्ला, भोक्ता र द्रष्टा दुवै भएको र विचारलाई समाख्याता आफैले प्रस्तुत गरेको साथै शशी एक्कल केन्द्रण रहको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: The present article is concerned with the analysis of narratological theoretical concepts in the story 'Chitako Jwala' written by Guru Prasad Mainali. In this, how the narrator is identified and in what form narrative voice is manifested are examined. An effort has been made to seek a solution to the inquiry of how narrative focalization is presented. Since the story is analyzed on the basis of theoretical assumptions of narratology, a deductive method has been utilized. In this, what has been said and who said it have been identified. An exploration has been conducted as to whether the narrator is inside or outside the text, is present as a character himself, or has made others present. In the text, a determination has been made regarding whether the narrator exists as an observer, an experiencer, or in both forms. Thus, in the present study, the conclusion is drawn that in Mainali's story 'Chitako Jwala', the narrator is first-person, specifically extradiegetic within first-person, open, both an experiencer and an observer, that ideas are presented by the narrator himself, and that Shashi is the single focalization.

informal_english: This article is all about analysing narratological theoretical concepts in the story 'Chitako Jwala' written by Guru Prasad Mainali. In this, how the narrator is identified and in what form narrative voice is manifested get examined. An effort has been made to sort out the query of how narrative focalisation is presented. Because the story is analysed on the basis of theoretical assumptions of narratology, a deductive method has been utilized. In this, what has been said and who said it have been sorted out. A proper search has been made into whether the narrator is inside or outside the text, is knocking about as a character himself, or has brought others onto the scene. In the text, it has been worked out whether the narrator exists as an observer, an experiencer, or in both roles. Thus, in the present study, the conclusion reached is that in Mainali's story 'Chitako Jwala', the narrator is first-person, specifically extradiegetic within first-person, open, both an experiencer and an observer, with ideas presented by the narrator himself, and Shashi being the sole focalisation.
